record.paper_title: Open problems, questions and challenges in finite-dimensional integrable systems
record.original_question: Find natural examples of integrable systems in classical me chanics with non-trivial Duistermaat-Chern classes.

evidence.quote: Problem 6.8 (S. V u Ngo. c). Find natural examples of integrable systems in classical me chanics with non-trivial Duistermaat-Chern classes.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,\omega)$ be a connected symplectic $2n$-manifold and let $F=(f_1,\dots,f_n):M\to\mathbb{R}^n$ be a completely integrable Hamiltonian system, i.e. the components $f_i$ are smooth functions in involution $\{f_i,f_j\}=0$ that are functionally independent on an open dense subset. Restrict to the set of regular values of $F$ whose fiber is a compact connected Lagrangian torus; by the Arnold–Liouville theorem $F$ defines a locally trivial Lagrangian $T^n$-fibration over this regular base $B^{\mathrm{reg}}$. Associated to this fibration are two Duistermaat invariants: the monodromy representation $\pi_1(B^{\mathrm{reg}})\to GL(n,\mathbb{Z})$, and, once the monodromy is killed (or after passing to an appropriate cover), the Lagrangian Chern class in $H^2(B^{\mathrm{reg}};\mathcal{Z})$ (with coefficients in the sheaf of integral affine sections) which obstructs the existence of a global Lagrangian section, the so-called Duistermaat–Chern class.

Problem: Exhibit a natural example of a completely integrable Hamiltonian system arising in classical mechanics (in the sense of a physically motivated system on a phase space coming from mechanics, e.g. rigid-body, celestial-mechanics, or molecular systems) whose Duistermaat–Chern class is non-trivial.
artifact.status_search_result: Available literature on monodromy and topology of integrable Hamiltonian systems indicates that while artificial examples with non-trivial Duistermaat–Chern class can be constructed (e.g. by twisting ruled symplectic 4-manifolds), no naturally occurring example from classical mechanics with a non-trivial Duistermaat–Chern class appears to be known. The problem is thus still open.

status_evidence.title: Symplectic topology of integrable Hamiltonian systems, II
status_evidence.snippet: Artificial examples with non-trivial Chern class can be constructed by twisting ruled symplectic 4-manifolds; no natural mechanical example is known.
status_evidence.claim: No natural classical-mechanics example with non-trivial Duistermaat–Chern class is currently known.

status_evidence.title: Recent advances in the monodromy theory of integrable Hamiltonian systems
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of monodromy in concrete integrable systems (spherical pendulum, Lagrange top, etc.); discusses obstructions including Duistermaat-type invariants.
status_evidence.claim: Concrete mechanical systems exhibit non-trivial monodromy but Chern-class non-triviality remains unestablished for natural mechanical models.
